commitResults.messageBody:
Summarize the required SE-EDU Git and Java coding standards in project-local reference documents.

These references give future code changes a consistent style baseline.

Currently, Alfred does not save tasks between sessions.

This should change as users lose their task list whenever the program exits.

Saves task-list changes immediately and load saved tasks at startup.

Uses a relative, OS-independent data path so the application works on
any computer and creates its data directory only when needed.

The saved format preserves task types, statuses, descriptions, and
deadline or event details.

UI cases share a working directory, which allows saved task data to affect later cases.

This makes the test results dependent on their execution order.

Run every case in its own temporary directory and support a setup session
followed by a fresh restart-verification session.

This isolates cases while testing that saved task state is loaded correctly
after Alfred restarts.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add instruction within AGENTS.md to follow coding conventions
Add date-time support for deadline and event tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Store task dates as LocalDateTime so deadlines and events can be
validated, displayed consistently, and restored after a restart.

Accept yyyy-MM-dd and d/M/yyyy HHmm inputs, and add UI coverage
for valid formatting and invalid-date state preservation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Updated the ASCII art to include the batman logo as well
commitResults.messageBody: Currently, the ASCII art only included the word 'Alfred' and this might have been confusing to understand the context

Alfred mixed command processing with all console input and output,
which made its main method responsible for unrelated concerns.

Move the banner, command reading, task responses, separators, and
error display into Ui. This gives later Parser and TaskList extractions
a smaller coordinator to work with while preserving all user-visible
behavior.

Alfred directly owned the mutable task ArrayList, so collection
operations were spread across the application coordinator, user
interface, and storage boundary.

Introduce TaskList to encapsulate ordered task access and mutation.
Update Alfred, Ui, and Storage to depend on this domain abstraction,
while retaining the existing task order and persistent format.

Alfred contained command recognition, task-number validation, and
task-construction rules alongside application coordination.

Move those input-interpretation responsibilities into Parser. Alfred
now receives parsed command details and focuses on task updates,
storage, and user-interface coordination without altering responses.

The existing Command enum represented only recognized keywords, but the
stretch-goal design needs Command to represent executable behavior.

Rename the enum to CommandType so it continues to model input labels.
This prepares a separate Command abstraction for later increments
without changing any parsing or user-visible behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add executable list and exit commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Alfred still handled the list and exit command behaviors directly,
which prevented the command hierarchy from owning even its simplest
actions.

Introduce the Command abstraction and extract ListCommand and
ExitCommand. Parser creates these argument-free commands, while the
existing dispatcher continues to handle commands that need arguments.

Alfred still performed task-status changes and persistence directly,
duplicating the command execution pattern used by the new framework.

Add MarkCommand and UnmarkCommand, with Parser validating their task
numbers before creating them. This moves both status-update behaviors
into executable commands while retaining their existing responses.

Alfred still removed tasks, saved the updated list, and displayed the
removal response directly.

Add DeleteCommand and let Parser validate its task number before
creating it. This moves the final indexed task mutation into the
command hierarchy while preserving deletion behavior and messages.

Alfred still added parsed tasks, saved them, and displayed confirmation
directly after the other commands had moved into the command hierarchy.

Add a generic AddCommand and have Parser create it for to-do, deadline,
and event input. Alfred now consistently parses and executes a Command
for every supported user instruction.

Alfred's static main method still created every collaborator and contained
the application loop, even after commands became executable objects.

Give Alfred instance fields and a run method that loads tasks and
executes one parsed command per loop iteration. Use finally for the
response separator so exit output remains unchanged.

All application classes are in the default package, which obscures
their responsibilities and prevents a clearer project structure.

Organize application classes by responsibility under the alfred
base package.

Update the UI test runner to compile recursive source paths and
launch the packaged application entry point.

commitResults.messageTitle: Edited build.gradle to run UI tests through Gradle
commitResults.messageBody: Added the uiTest task and made Gradle's test task run the existing console UI test plan

commitResults.messageTitle: Add parser and storage JUnit tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Cover core command parsing and task persistence behavior, including
invalid input and malformed saved data.

Allow Storage to use an injected file path so tests run in isolated
temporary directories. Fix malformed deadline and event commands so
they return validation errors instead of throwing index exceptions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Package Alfred as executable fat JAR
commitResults.messageBody:
Configure the Shadow plugin output as alfred.jar and document how
to build, locate, distribute, and run the executable JAR.

Users cannot locate tasks by a keyword when their list grows. Add the
find command to match task descriptions case-insensitively and display
matching tasks in list order.

Reject missing search keywords to preserve clear command feedback. Include
JUnit and console UI coverage for matching, no-match, and invalid inputs.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap project text and refine Gradle ignores
commitResults.messageBody:
Project source, documentation, scripts, and test-plan text contain lines
over the 110-character limit. The ignore rules also exclude build.gradle,
which is version-controlled build configuration.

Wrap maintained content at 110 characters or fewer, using language-specific
continuations where needed. Keep Gradle caches and build output ignored, but
track build.gradle so build configuration changes are captured in Git.

Use formatting-only changes to preserve behavior while making the project
consistent with the configured editor limit.

The project lacks automated enforcement of the required Java style rules.
Add the SE-EDU Checkstyle configuration and Gradle tasks to detect violations.

Reformat affected production and test code to satisfy the configured rules.
Use the AddressBook Level 3 configuration because it matches the project’s
required Java coding standard.

Alfred only starts through its console entry point, so it has no graphical
application to extend in later milestones.
Add the JavaFX launcher and initial Hello World window.
Configure JavaFX dependencies for all supported platforms and document the
manual GUI verification step.

Alfred needs a structured interface before it can process commands through
JavaFX.
Add a scrollable dialog area, sample dialog, text field, Send button, and
avatar resources.
Keep the controls non-interactive because command handling begins in Part 3.

The chat layout does not yet respond to user input.
Handle Enter and Send events to append user and Alfred dialogs.
Auto-scroll the conversation so the newest response remains visible.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor JavaFX views to use FXML
commitResults.messageBody:
The chat layout and dialog structure are embedded in Java classes, which
makes visual changes difficult to isolate.
Move the main window and dialog layouts into FXML with dedicated controllers.
Keep existing chat interaction intact while separating view and control code.

The chat controls do not adapt to a resized window and use the default
JavaFX appearance.
Anchor the layout controls and add CSS for Alfred-themed chat styling.
Keep the existing interaction behavior unchanged while improving usability.

commitResults.messageTitle: Connect JavaFX chat to Alfred commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The GUI cannot yet process task commands or greet users when it opens.
Route chat input through Alfred's parser, storage, and command handling, then
show the resulting response in the dialog area.

Add Alfred's startup greeting so the JavaFX experience matches the CLI.
Capture GUI output through the existing UI layer to preserve the CLI behavior
while keeping command processing shared between both interfaces.

The GUI does not close after a valid  command, and unknown-command
errors refer to Alfred in the third person.

Close the window after briefly displaying the farewell response. Use a
first-person error message so Alfred speaks directly to the user.

Add regression coverage and update the UI test plan for both behaviors.

Task-list access and task serialization rely on internal contracts that
otherwise fail later as null dereferences, invalid indices, or bad casts.

Assert those programmer-owned contracts at their boundaries and enable
assertions in the standard Gradle test and run paths. Keep user input and
saved-file errors as exceptions because assertions can be disabled.

Add focused tests and documentation to verify and explain the assertions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertion guidance to agent instructions
commitResults.messageBody:
Future Java changes need a consistent distinction between programmer assumptions and invalid external input. Without that guidance, agents can either omit useful safeguards or use assertions where validation is required.

Direct agents to maintain assertions for meaningful internal contracts and to handle user and file errors with validation and exceptions. Keep the rule in AGENTS.md so it applies to future changes.

Command parsing relies on raw marker text and numeric offsets. Those values obscure where each command argument begins and make future syntax changes easy to apply inconsistently.

Name the command markers and derive offsets from their lengths. Extract the shared command-argument operation so the parser states its intent without changing command behavior.

List and find each maintain their own loop for displaying one-based task numbers. Keeping two copies risks formatting drift as the task display evolves.

Extract the shared numbered-task display operation and retain each command's distinct heading. This removes duplication while preserving the established console output.

Command recognition uses null to signal an unknown command, which hides a valid parser state and requires callers to infer its meaning.

Represent that state with CommandType.UNKNOWN and reject it at the command-dispatch boundary. Add a control-flow assertion and unit test so unknown input remains explicit while user-facing error output is unchanged.

The console and GUI paths both parse and execute commands independently. Maintaining those copies can cause one interface to diverge from the other.

Extract the common command execution operation and keep UI-specific response handling at each call site. Assert that task loading precedes execution so the shared precondition is documented.

Storage parsing and serialization embed record type codes, completion values, and field positions directly in control flow. Those literals hide the saved-file format and make maintenance error-prone.

Name the format's separators, codes, statuses, counts, and field positions. Preserve the exact serialized representation so existing task files remain compatible.

commitResults.messageTitle: TaskList: Filter matching tasks with streams
commitResults.messageBody:
Task searching uses a manual loop to select descriptions matching a keyword. The loop is correct, but it obscures the operation as a filter followed by collection.

Replace the loop with a stream filter and collect its encounter-ordered results into an ArrayList. Keep the existing mutable result and case-insensitive behavior so callers observe no change.
Add assertions for task-list invariants

The Assertions increment updates storage serialization contracts, while Code Quality names the same storage format values. The parallel branches therefore conflict in the task serialization path.

Combine the assertions with the named storage constants while synchronizing this branch with master. This preserves both increments before the Code Quality pull request is merged.
Improve code quality
Filter matching tasks with streams

Alfred has no way to view time-based tasks in chronological order,
making it harder to review upcoming deadlines and events.

Add sort commands for ascending and descending chronological views.
Keep sorting display-only so existing task numbers, insertion order, and
saved data remain unchanged.

Place date-less to-dos consistently at the end of ascending views and
the start of descending views, preserving their relative order.

Master does not include the C-Sort extension, so users cannot view tasks chronologically.

Merge the tested display-only sort feature into master. Keep the branch merge
explicit so the extension's development history remains visible.
